Subject: OliveAI: SDK prefetch stalls with long-context workloads - initial report

Team —

Quick heads-up: OliveAI (contact: Amanda Chen) is hitting a reproducible stall when using our Python SDK prefetch/kv-cache with requests that have ~6k tokens of context. They see the request hang (no streaming tokens) for ~10–20s, then a burst of the remaining tokens. Customer is using Redwood Hosted with our default model routing and SDK v0.9.1.

Symptoms provided: intermittent stalls only when prefix length > ~4k tokens, appears more frequent under higher concurrency. They pasted screenshots and attached a short log.

Asks: can Platform/Runtime prioritise initial triage and a patch candidate? This is blocking a demo later this week. If we can get a short-term workaround they can apply from the SDK, that would buy us time.

I’ve included the logs and their minimal repro snippet (attached). Please advise next steps and whether this should be treated P1 for Hosted customers.

Thanks,
Vanessa
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: repro_log.txt, sdk_snippet.py, screenshot-err.png

Subject: Re: OliveAI: SDK prefetch stalls with long-context workloads - initial report

Thanks Vanessa — forwarding to runtime on-call and starting investigation. A couple quick asks to speed this up:

1) Can Marissa push the exact SDK version, model name, and a minimal reproducible script (we need a single-run case that triggers the hang)? The attached snippet from the customer looks close but I want something we can run in our infra.
2) Please zip and share the tracing header (X-Request-Id) if possible — we can correlate to serving logs.

Hypothesis: looks like an edge case in our prefetch + kv-cache logic when the prefix crosses the LRU/segment boundary; could be a kernel scheduling stall where the runtime spins waiting for an absent kv segment and prefetch retries cause starvation. If so, a short-term SDK change to disable prefetch or reduce prefetch window should unblock them. Longer-term runtime fix may be a guard to avoid re-entrant prefetch under certain cache-miss conditions.

I'm marking this P1 for triage on-call. Will post updates in this thread.

—Dev

Dev / Vanessa —

Copied an internal reproducer here and attached the logs you asked for. Reproducer notes:
- SDK: python-redwood 0.9.1 (pip)
- Model: rdw-mix-13B-v1 (hosted)
- Concurrency: 6 parallel workers, each sending ~6k-token prefix + 512-gen

Minimal repro (sdk_snippet.py attached) — core part below:

\"\"\"python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=\"REDACTED\")
ctx = 'A' * 6000  # long prefix to force larger kv usage
for i in range(6):
    resp = client.completions.create(model=\"rdw-mix-13B-v1\", prompt=ctx, max_tokens=512, streaming=False, prefetch=True)
    print(len(resp.text))
\"\"\"

Observed: runs sometimes hang at call (no HTTP 200 until 12–20s), then a flood of tokens. The attached repro_log.txt has request IDs and a few stack samples from the client side. I also included a server trace for one of the request IDs (INF-2248) — I’ve redacted internal hostnames.

Temporary client workaround that consistently avoids the hang: set prefetch=False or reduce prefetch_window to 512. That reduces throughput but is acceptable short-term for their demo.

Marissa
Field Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: OliveAI: SDK prefetch stalls with long-context workloads - initial report

Update after triage: we reproduced locally with Marissa's snippet. Root cause summary: prefetch state machine can re-enter during async kv fetch miss on certain segment boundaries, which leads to scheduling contention and a long blocking wait before the runtime flushes and resumes token generation. The blocking window matches the customer's observed 10–20s stall.

Short-term mitigation (can ship within 48 hours as a canary):
- Runtime: add a guard to detect re-entrant prefetch triggers and serialize them (no behavioral change unless the edge case occurs). Patch: INF-2248-rlv1.
- SDK: add a simple toggle to disable prefetch by default for requests with prefix_length > 4096 (config flag prefetch_auto_disable) so hosted customers get safer defaults while we roll runtime fix.

Plan / timeline:
- Today: land runtime guard on a nightly canary build and run regression harness (by EOD).
- +48h: canary rollout to 5% of Hosted traffic and validation against OliveAI repro.
- +7 days: full rollout if no regressions. Backport to Dedicated hosts in a patch release afterwards.

Marissa — please confirm the SDK change is trivial to ship (toggle + release note). Vanessa / Sergio — please hold communications to OliveAI; we’ll ask them to toggle prefetch_auto_disable while we run the canary. If they are uncomfortable, Sergio suggested offering credits; we can finalize externally.

I’ll open the runtime PR and link it here.

—Dev
